resolution.note:
Both refuters killed every blocking finding, so the row stamps PASS:verify-refuted and this REVISE stays as the record. pedagogy §27 line 87: harm: The judge's facts check out, but the finding doesn't hold up as a blocking defect once the harm lens is applied.

Verified facts. L87 reads exactly as quoted. The maintainer block (L99-118) has no accept-note naming any §27 carve-out. git blame puts L87 in a9d3e1d5, the 2026-10-07 first build of the full training. That is generated build text, not wording the maintainer supplied. The letter of §27 is breached: "reads out" and "say so out loud" are a specified utterance at a scheduled beat. I grant that.

Why it doesn't survive:

(b) The harm is a restatement of the rule. "§27 gives that to the trainer… a cue without the note is still a violation" describes the rule. It names nobody who ends up worse off. APT101 is a trio-as-one-unit training with no self-study variant. The strategy doc says the training "treats them as one unit". So §27's "to whom?" problem doesn't arise: the addressee is the other two seats at the table. The trainer still owns the stop: the maintainer block says "Phase 5 turns into a debate → the trainer stops it at three minutes."

(a) This is arguably a group round under check_workshop.md, which fires per beat when the output belongs to the group, and its trigger names "a group round". Comparing three seats' memories can't happen without the room. Sibling judges in this same batch passed the same kind of line on that reasoning: write-the-bet L49 "Read the three out loud", what-goes-in L45 "Go through each kind of material out loud", and choose-the-bet. Blocking it here only is inconsistent tidiness.

(c) Both proposed fixes fail under the rule's own carve-out conditions. Fix 1 adds an accept-note naming the second carve-out. That carve-out requires a Debrief or Human-close slot named in the strategy arc. The build plan marks beat 6 as "Control", and the strategy doc names no such slot, so the note would be false. Fix 2 cuts L87 to a third-carve-out line. That carve-out needs all four tells, including "no cue" and offer grammar. A scheduled "Phase 5" heading can't meet "no cue", so the only rule-clean outcome is deleting the phase. Deleting it removes a deliberate designed beat. The maintainer block's Role moves say "Phase 5 lays the three memories side by side without settling the disagreement". It also breaks the "Three memories, one bet, three seats" through-line from L9 to the take-stock at L93. That costs more than the defect.

At most this is a non-blocking maintainer note: record an accept-note, or decide whether APT101 trio rounds get their own carve-out. It is not a body edit.; pedagogy §45 line 99: harm: The judge's facts check out. I ran grep -n -i leap on curriculum/exercises/apt101-build-your-product-memory.md and got 0 hits. The maintainer block opens at L99 (<!-- maintainer -->) and runs to the View summary at L118. The sibling apt101-paint-the-product-box.md does carry "**Leap test:**" at L152. §45 (check_pedagogy.md L115) does say every exercise maintainer block needs a leap test.

The finding still fails the harm lens.

(b) The harm is the rule restated, not a consequence. "The story judge cannot check that the exercise changes behaviour" just says the rule's own check has no label to read.

(d) Other lines already carry the meaning, so the fix only relabels them. The judge proposes the artefact-led carve-out: name the artefact the student now owns and uses. That sentence is already in the block:
- View summary (L118): "The artefact is three personal memories every agent reads from here on."
- Artefacts: "produces sources/, memory/ (cited topic pages, memory/index.md), memory/soft-pages.md, all personal ... Read by apt101-send-it-off and every Day 2 prompt."
- Role in Day 1: "Day 2's overnight digest and every Day 2 prompt read it."

The trainer also has observable outcomes to test the room against. The body's take-stock section asks each person to name one sharp page and one soft page, and soft-pages.md is a concrete file they produce. So "the trainer has nothing to test the room against" is false.

(a) Nobody in the room is worse off. This is maintainer-only apparatus, the outcomes exist under other labels, and the block already passed behavior at dd243e74.

The fix would add a Leap test line that restates the View summary in the carve-out's form. That is tidiness, not repair of a defect. Uncertainty defaults to refuted.; pedagogy §47 line 114: harm: The judge counted correctly: L114 names failure modes for Phases 1, 3 and 5 only, and Phases 2 and 4 have no maintainer-block entry. That literal gap is real. The harm claim does not hold up, though.

(1) The Phase 1 plan-approval part is wrong under the rule. §47 asks for one dominant failure mode and one escape hatch per phase, not one per forcing function. L114 already gives Phase 1 two of each: ingest runs long → cap at ten; material outside the door creeps in → check the plan line against team/what-goes-in.md. L49 also carries the plan-approval steer in the body ("If two topics should be one, say so. If the riskiest assumption from the bet has no topic, ask for one. Then approve.").

(2) The failures the judge predicts for Phases 2 and 4 are already blocked inside the prompts the students paste. That is lens (d): another line already carries the meaning. For Phase 2, the judge predicts an under-flagged list. Prompt build-your-challenge-memory-4 says "Assume at least one of the three has a generic top claim. Name it... If on re-reading all three are specific, say why, and name the sentence most at risk of slipping generic." Under-flagging is ruled out by construction. For Phase 4, the judge predicts all six issues approved. Prompt build-your-challenge-memory-8 says "name the one you're least sure is real... that's the one I should scrutinize first. Don't apply anything yet. Ask me to approve or reject each one." Body L81 adds "Approve some, reject some." The recovery move the judge says the trainer lacks is already in the prompt.

(3) Lens (a): nobody in the room is worse off. These are 5-minute and 4-minute phases whose prompts recover their own failures. The finding's sentence "The trainer has no recovery move" restates the rule's wording about a missing maintainer-block line; it names no consequence for anyone in the room. That is lens (b).

(4) The precedent points the same way. The AE101 source exercise (curriculum/exercises/build-your-challenge-memory.md L178) uses the same prompts -4 and -8 and also lists no watch-for for the audit or review step. This is a deliberate reuse of prompts built to guard themselves, not an extraction leak.

The leftover issue is a tidiness note: §47 would be met word for word by one more maintainer-block clause. It is not a BLOCKING defect.; pedagogy §48 line 21: harm: I'm refuting this, though not with full confidence. On the letter, the judge is right: check_pedagogy.md §48 (core memory, line 121) asks the callout to "name the premature-stop failure explicitly," and the L21 callout in curriculum/exercises/apt101-build-your-product-memory.md covers only over-reading. The case for BLOCKING is weaker than the finding makes it look, for four reasons.

(1) The stated harm mostly repeats the rule. The scenario of "a memory built from 3 of 10 sources would read as finished" is invented, not observed. The file's own maintainer block records behavior PASS @dd243e74 with sim traces bound (commit 84ea21e3), and no run trace shows a shallow memory build.

(2) The read is small and already guarded. Prompt 3 (curriculum/prompts/build-your-challenge-memory-3.md) reads "every real-content file in sources/," which L39 caps at eight to ten items. That is a short list, not a read-the-world sweep. It also runs under plan mode (L43), which §48 itself calls "the primary control." L49 then has the student check the plan's topic split and ask for a topic if the riskiest assumption has none, so a plan built on too few sources gets caught there. The every-claim-cites-a-source rule in prompt 3 makes coverage visible too. Prompt 8 is deliberately bounded ("up to six," "an empty category is a valid finding"), so a short answer is the designed outcome, not a premature stop.

(3) Precedent. The A101 exercise this one reuses by key, curriculum/exercises/build-your-challenge-memory.md L25, has the same over-reading-only callout. It passed pedagogy on 2026-08-25 (pedagogy@725101ec), after the "premature stop" clause landed (git log -S finds it around 2026-07-26 to 2026-08-02). So a pedagogy judge has already accepted this callout shape on this exact prompt sequence with the rule in force.

(4) Cost. The fix adds student-facing prose to a 45-minute beat, and recorded maintainer feedback says additions on curriculum line-reads are near-auto-reject. At most this is a non-blocking suggestion, not a BLOCK.
